partnershipPlan: Two people with lived experience of admission and harmful drinking review the screening wording, the session materials and the follow-up script; the community alcohol team reviews the referral route.
socialListening: No social media listening; the ward's patient feedback forms for the last year are read for comments about how staff raised alcohol.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: On the first night I would have said anything to be left alone; a week later I wanted to talk about it.
items.implication: Screen once the patient is well enough, not at admission.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase (named nurse): Twenty minutes is fine if nobody is in seclusion; the pocket card keeps me on track when I am interrupted.
items.implication: Keep sessions short and support fidelity with the card.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: He left with a plan on paper and no number to ring when the weekend came.
items.implication: Give a named contact and a referral route before discharge.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: It helped that she asked what I wanted to change instead of telling me I drink too much.
items.implication: Keep the motivational style central in training refreshers.

summary: Four composite voices on timing, ward pressure, discharge and tone.
